label: NHRP
notes: NHRP control-plane header per RFC 2332, carried directly over IP protocol 54 (the number IANA lists for NARP; it is also how Wireshark registers its NHRP dissector) and, in DMVPN deployments, inside GRE -- the window only matches NHRP-relative offsets, so both encapsulations filter identically once the packet reaches the NHRP header. The 20-byte fixed header (RFC 2332 section 5.1) and the 8-byte mandatory common header (section 5.2.0.1) sit at fixed offsets for every packet type and are fully modelled: 14 field views plus one reasoned exclusion. Everything from byte 28 on is variable-length and outside fixed-offset filtering: the source NBMA address and subaddress bounded by shtl/sstl, the source and destination protocol addresses bounded by src_proto_len/dst_proto_len, the CIE list and the extension TLVs. The 5-byte ar$pro.snap is excluded because over IP the short Ethertype form of ar$pro.type is mandatory (section 5.1), so those bytes are always zero, and a 5-byte field exceeds the 4-byte BPF load window anyway. The Flags word is labelled with Resolution Request/Reply semantics; Registration messages use only the top bit (as the Uniqueness bit, section 5.2.3) and Purge messages only the top bit (as the N bit, section 5.2.5), and in Error and Traffic Indications bytes 22-27 are repurposed as unused/error code/error offset -- the offsets themselves are unchanged, so request_id still matches those messages as a raw word. Op type 8 (Traffic Indication) and the NAT flag bit are Cisco DMVPN extensions (I-D draft-detienne-dmvpn-01) documented by Wireshark's dissector, not RFC 2332.

fields.label: Address Family Number
fields.description: Family of the NBMA addresses carried in the mandatory part (the RFC 1700 address family numbers). An mGRE/DMVPN cloud uses 1 with shtl 4: the NBMA address is the tunnel endpoint's public IPv4 address.

fields.label: Protocol Type
fields.description: Coding of the internetwork layer protocol: NLPIDs below 0x0100, Ethertypes from 0x0600, or 0x0080 to move the protocol ID into the 5-byte SNAP field. NHRP-for-IP always transmits the Ethertype coding 0x0800, which is what makes ar$pro.snap zero.

fields.label: Hop Count
fields.description: Maximum number of NHSs the packet may traverse, used like an IP TTL; each transit NHS decrements it and exceeding it triggers an Error Indication (code 15).

fields.label: Packet Size
fields.description: Total length of the NHRP packet in octets including the fixed header, excluding the link-layer encapsulation; 20 is the minimum legal value.

fields.label: Checksum
fields.description: Standard IP checksum over the entire NHRP packet starting at the fixed header, computed as if a zero byte were appended to odd-length packets.

fields.label: Extension Offset
fields.description: Offset from the start of the NHRP packet of the first extension TLV; 0 means the packet carries no extensions. Error Indications never carry extensions.

fields.label: Version
fields.description: Version of the generic address mapping and management protocol: 1 is NHRP as defined by RFC 2332, 0 is the multicast address resolution server protocol.

fields.label: NHRP Packet Type
fields.description: NHRP packet type when version is 1. Types 1-6 are the DMVPN workhorses: spoken nodes send Registration Requests to their NHS and Resolution Requests for distant tunnel endpoints; 7 reports errors; 8 (not in RFC 2332, a Cisco DMVPN extension) redirects traffic onto a shortcut.

fields.label: Source NBMA Address Type/Length
fields.description: Type and length of the source NBMA address in one byte: bit 0x40 selects native E.164 format (0 means NSAP or the technology's native form), the low 6 bits give the length in octets (4 for the IPv4 NBMA address of an mGRE tunnel endpoint), and the top bit is reserved and sent as zero.

fields.label: Source NBMA Subaddress Type/Length
fields.description: Same type/length encoding for the source NBMA subaddress; always 0 over IP-based NBMA networks, which have no subaddress concept, so no storage follows it in the mandatory part.

fields.label: Source Protocol Address Length
fields.description: Length in octets of the source protocol address that follows the common header; 4 for IPv4, 16 for IPv6.

fields.label: Destination Protocol Address Length
fields.description: Length in octets of the destination protocol address; the address an NHC registers with or asks to resolve.

fields.label: Flags
fields.description: Message-type-specific flags occupying the word at offset 22. Labels follow Resolution Request/Reply semantics (RFC 2332 sections 5.2.1-5.2.2): Q requester is a router, A only authoritative answers wanted/reply is authoritative, D destination binding stable for the holding time, U unique binding, S source binding stable. Registration messages define only the top bit (as Uniqueness, section 5.2.3) and Purge messages only the top bit (as no-Purge-Reply-expected, section 5.2.5); NAT (0x0002) is the Cisco DMVPN extension bit, not RFC 2332. Error and Traffic Indications leave the word unused.

fields.label: Request ID
fields.description: Counter value that, with the source protocol address, matches replies to their requests; copied verbatim from a request into its reply. In Error Indications bytes 24-25 carry the error code and 26-27 the error offset instead (section 5.2.7), and in Traffic Indications bytes 24-25 carry the traffic code.

excluded.reason: ar$pro.snap, the 5-byte SNAP long-form protocol ID (RFC 2332 §5.1): it exceeds the 4-byte BPF load window, and over IP protocol 54 it is always zero because section 5.1 mandates the short Ethertype form of ar$pro.type whenever one exists
